Closed the verbatim-thread tail gap. /end's step-5 transcript copy ran mid-close, so every persisted thread (and cb:b540's verbatim rule) structurally under-captured its own closing turns - the report, the commit, any post-/end continuation; this session's copy landed ~2% short of the live log. Two-phase fix: /end now defers the byte-copy to step-7-last (latest-possible in-close snapshot) and drops a per-session finalize-marker (~/.claude/transcript-pending/<id>.json); a new SessionEnd hook (cb-finalize-transcript.sh, dotfiles-claude) re-copies the COMPLETE log to the homed destination and commits it at true session end. The in-/end copy is the crash fallback - SessionEnd does not fire on crash. This is the cb:a165 procedural->structural move applied to /end's own persistence: stop having the agent copy its still-being-written log from inside it.

Reversed the SessionEnd-hook approach recorded in this node's prior evidence. The hook + marker + SessionStart recovery + concurrency guard was too much fragile machinery for ~1-2 closing turns of no decision content, and it produced a concurrency bug plus a destructive test that swept live state (agent-behavior:a108). Removed entirely (dotfiles 952c302). Replaced with: /end copies the transcript as late as possible (step 7, last write before commit) - the verifiable in-session record. Turns after it (the close, or work done after /end) are captured by re-running /end; the operator accepted that trade. The SessionStart desk hook (cb-desk.sh) stays. Lesson: a structural fix is not automatically better - here it added more failure surface than the 1-2-turn gap it closed.
